notes.markdown:
## Timestamp choice in replication

1. Client one wants to update the value associated with key x to v1 with a logical timestamp t1.[^203][^204][^205][^206]
2. Concurrently, client two wants to set the value of key x to v2 with a logical timestamp t2.[^207][^208][^209]
3. Replica a receives the request from client two first, then receives the request from client one.[^210]
4. Replica b receives the requests in the opposite order: first from client one, then from client two.[^211][^212]
5. The replicas cannot use the order in which they see the requests to determine whether v1 or v2 is the final value, because they would end up in different states and inconsistent at the end.[^213][^214][^215][^216]
6. All replicas must end up in the same state in a replicated system, and timestamps provide the relative ordering of operations needed to ensure consistent state across replicas.[^217][^218][^219][^220]

- Last writer wins is a resolution policy where the value with the higher timestamp is kept and lower timestamps are overwritten.[^221][^222][^223][^224][^225][^226][^227][^228]
- Last writer wins discards data by overwriting values with lower timestamps and forgetting them entirely.[^229][^230][^231][^232][^233]
- Vector clocks are incomparable when generated for concurrent operations, allowing detection of concurrent updates.[^234][^235][^236][^237]
- Using vector clocks, a value is only overwritten by another value if the vector timestamps show the later one is strictly greater than the earlier one.[^238][^239]
- When concurrent updates are detected using vector clocks, multiple values can be kept for a single key and returned to the application for conflict resolution.[^240][^241][^242][^243][^244][^245]
- An application can have explicit logic for conflict resolution to combine information from concurrent updates into a single value and avoid losing data.[^246][^247][^248][^249][^250][^251]
- Different database systems make different choices between totally ordered Lamport timestamps and partially ordered vector timestamps depending on what behavior is appropriate for their applications.[^252][^253][^254][^255]

cheatSheet.markdown:
## Request delivery semantics
- At most once: Request sent once without retries; may or may not arrive.[^42][^43][^44]
- At least once: Retry until acknowledgement received; request may arrive multiple times.[^45][^46]
- Exactly once: Operation takes effect exactly once despite retries and message loss.[^47][^48][^49]
- Exactly once with idempotence: Retry idempotent operations to achieve exactly once semantics.[^50][^51]
- Exactly once with deduplication: Store requests that have happened to achieve exactly once.[^52][^53]
